sections.title: Surgical Entry: The Anatomy of Access

branches: Phakic: 4.0 mm from limbus (protects crystalline lens)
Angle: 5-30 degree bi-planar entry for self-sealing
Location: Usually Superotemporal, Superonasal, and Inferotemporal

sections.title: Fluidics: Vacuum vs. Flow Control
content: Duty Cycle: Proportion of time port is open. High duty cycle = more efficient shaving.
Cut Rate: Modern vitrectors reach 7,500 - 20,000 cpm. Higher rates reduce retinal traction/tug.
Venturini (Vacuum): Footpedal controls suction directly. Faster response for PVD induction.
Peristaltic (Flow): Footpedal controls flow rate. More stable for delicate peeling near the retina.

sections.title: Standard PPV Procedural Workflow
content: Step 1: Trocar insertion & Infusion line placement (Verify tip is in vitreous cavity).
Step 2: Core Vitrectomy: High cut rate, moderate vacuum to clear central opacities.
Step 3: Posterior Vitreous Detachment (PVD) Induction: Use suction or Triesence to lift the hyaloid.
Step 4: Peripheral Shave: Scleral depression to remove vitreous base (critical in RD cases).
Step 5: Endolaser / Cryotherapy: Treatment of retinal breaks or panretinal photocoagulation.
Step 6: Fluid-Air Exchange (FAX): Aspiration of subretinal/intravitreal fluid under air.
Step 7: Tamponade Injection: Gas (SF6, C3F8) or Silicone Oil.
Step 8: Port Removal & Massage: Check for leaks and suture if necessary.

sections.title: Inducing PVD: The 'Suction & Lift' Technique
content: Staining: Use Triamcinolone Acetonide (Triesence) to visualize the posterior hyaloid face.
Approach: Engage hyaloid over the optic nerve head where it is thickest.
Action: Apply 300-400 mmHg vacuum, lift slowly toward the center of the eye.
Sign: The 'Weiss Ring' confirms detachment of the peripapillary glial tissue.

sections.title: RED FLAGS: Intraoperative Emergencies
content: Suprachoroidal Hemorrhage: Sudden hardening of eye, 'darkening' of red reflex.
Subretinal Infusion: Retina billows up immediately upon starting infusion.
Iatrogenic Retinal Break: Usually occurs during peripheral shave or PVD induction.
Lens Touch: Immediate cataract formation (whitening of the lens cortex).
High IOP: Risk of Central Retinal Artery Occlusion (CRAO) if infusion is too high for too long.

sections.title: Remember the '3 S's' of Gas Fill

content.explanation: Stay down (Positioning), See floaters (Bubble visualization), Scuba/Soar (No flying/diving while gas is in the eye).

sections.title: Key Clinical Pearls
content: The 'Silver Lining' Sign: Air-fluid interface helps find small peripheral breaks.
Avoid 'Cold' Laser: Ensure the laser spot has a slight grey-white uptake for permanent adhesion.
Trocars: Always check the valved cannulas for patency before insertion.
Ergonomics: Keep the patient's head level and your chair height set to avoid back strain during long cases.

sections.title: Complication Management
content: Port Leakage: Use 8-0 or 9-0 Vicryl/Monocryl if a 'wick' of vitreous is present or if pressure is low.
Persistent Macular Hole: Consider 'Inverted ILM Flap' technique or autologous blood patch.
Subretinal Gas: Ensure the break is completely flat and dry before finishing FAX.
Oil Emulsification: Remove silicone oil within 3-6 months if possible to prevent glaucoma.
